title: Which diseases medical AI benchmarks actually test
line: every question in nine public benchmarks, labelled by condition and coded to ICD-10-CM
question: When a model scores well on a medical benchmark, which diseases was it actually tested on, and which ones never come up?
data: MedQA, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, MMLU medical subjects, MedBullets, HealthBench

figures.note: the pipeline: collect 14,088 items, label each condition and its role with a local model, map names to ICD-10-CM through the official Alphabetic Index, check with two other models, then publish a searchable explorer.
tested conditions by ICD-10-CM chapter, stacked by benchmark. every chapter is covered, but unevenly: external causes of morbidity has fewer than ten items.

found: 14,088 unique items across nine public benchmarks; 5,000 of them (HealthBench) have no answer key, and are kept as coverage rather than scored.

names are never coded by the model itself. each condition goes through the official ICD-10-CM Alphabetic Index first, then fuzzy and embedding matches, and anything unmatched stays visible rather than dropping out of the counts.
calls: condition roles, not just mentions: tested, context, ruled out, or appearing only in a wrong option. a disease named in a distractor is not a disease the benchmark tests.
question text is withheld wherever a dataset's licence does not clearly allow redistribution; the explorer shows identifiers and derived labels instead.
everything runs on local models, so the whole index cost nothing in API fees and can be rerun by anyone.
not_shown: validation numbers are held for the paper in progress with Chris and Joon
